The Petitioners have filed the Petition against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.25,25,000/- for the death of P.Gangi Reddy in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The brief averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 20.06.2020 at about 7.30 p.m. the deceased P.Gangi Reddy was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-01- HG-7067 on Yerpedu-Venkatagiri main road, near HP petrol bunk, Vampalli Village, at the time, the driver of the lorry bearing No.TN-18-AU-4158 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the deceased from backside.
In the result, P.Gangi Reddy sustained grievous injuries to his head.
Immediately he was shifted to Area hospital, Srikalahasthi for treatment wherein doctor declared him brought dead.

Prior to the date of accident, the deceased P.Gangi Reddy was hale and healthy and was working as a progressive farmer and also doing civil contracts and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month from contracts and Rs.6,00,000/-p.a. in agriculture.
3. The Petitioners have further contended that the accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of lorry bearing No.TN-18-AU-4158 by its driver.

Respondent No.1 is the insurer P.Subba Ratnamma vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93742737/
2 and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the lorry

4. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 appeared before the court through its counsel and filed objections to the main petition.
Respondent No.2 remained absent and it was placed exparte.
In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.1, denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.

Further contended that the accident took place on account of involvement of two vehicles i.e., lorry and motor cycle and there is gross negligence on the part of the deceased who was riding the motor cycle.
Further contended that the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary party.
Further contended that the deceased was not holding valid driving licence and deceased himself dashed against the lorry.
He was not wearing any protective head gear/helmet while riding the two wheeler on the date of accident.
Further contended that it has issued policy in respect of lorry bearing No.TN-18-AU-4158 and it was valid on the date of accident.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
5. On the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor in office has framed following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that Gangi Reddy was died in the Road Traffic Accident which occurred on 20.06.2020 at about 7.30 p.m. on Yerpedu- Venkatagiri main road, near HP Petrol bunk, Vanpalli Village, Srikalahasthi (M) Chittoor (D)
Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-18-AU- 4158?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of Gangi Reddy?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4. What Order or Award?
6.
In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.3 got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 10 documents as per Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-10 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence.
But during the cross-examination of PW.1 one document was confronted and marked as Ex.R.1.
7. Heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioners and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1.

I have perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on P.Subba Ratnamma vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93742737/
3 record.
8.

My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has specifically denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry.
However, it has not examined the driver of lorry to prove the said contention.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.3 has been examined as P.W.1 and got marked 10 documents as per Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-10.

Ex .P-1 to Ex.P-6 are the certified copies of FIR,
Complaint, death intimation, Charge sheet, PM report and accident inspection report.

11. Upon going through the said documents, Ex.P1 and 2 i.e., FIR and Complaint, show that the case was registered against the driver of the offending lorry bearing No.TN-18-AU- 4158 by Tirupathi Urban Police for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304A of IPC.
Ex. P3.
Is the death intimation letter.
Ex . P.4
is the copy of Charge-sheet, which shows that the driver of lorry was charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304A of IPC.
Ex.P.5 is the PM report, which shows that cause of death is due to shock associate with infra cranial injury.
Ex.P.6 is the accident inspection report from Motor Vehicles inspector shows that accident is not due to any mechanical defects of the crime vehicles.

Ex.P.7 is the Certificate issued by Panchayat Secretary, Ex.P.8 is the translated copy of certificate, Ex.P.9 is the notarised copy of Patta passbook and Ex.P.10 is the notarised copy of Aadhar card of PW.1.
12. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 has cross examined the P.W.1 in lengthy.
In the cross-examination PW.1 has denied the suggestions and nothing could be elicited to disprove the contention of the Petitioners.
Moreover he is not an eye witness to the accident.
13. The owner of the lorry placed exparte, as such he has no defence.
Hence it is clear that he has admitted that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further though the Respondent No.1 denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry, but it has not produced cogent evidence to prove its contention.
Moreover the charge sheet is material document which shows that due to rash and negligence driving of the lorry the accident has occurred.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the said P.Subba Ratnamma vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93742737/
4 accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and the deceased P.Gangi Reddy succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Affirmative".
14. Issue No.2 and 3:
Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of the facts.
15.
It is stated in the Petitions that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are sons of the deceased P.Gangi Reddy.
In order to prove this fact, PW.1 has produced his Aadhar card at Ex.P.10.
In the cross examination aadhar card of deceased is confronted and marked as Ex.R.1.
Upon going through the same, it clearly shows the relationship of the deceased with the petitioner No.3.
They have not produced any documents to show the relationship of petitioner No.1 and 2 with deceased.
But there is no serious dispute about the relationship of the petitioner with deceased.
Hence, it is held that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased P.Gangi Reddy.

16. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 59 years and his avocation is shown as progressive farm and earning Rs.6,00,000/- p.a. and also doing civil contracts and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- p.m..
In this regard, they have produced Patta pass book to prove his avocation.
However, they have not produced any document to prove his income.
Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has occurred in the year 2020, notional income of Rs.14,500/- p.m. is taken for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
17. Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased P.Gangi Reddy as 59 years at the time of the accident.
But they have not produced any document.
In the cross-examination of PW.1 learned counsel for confronted copy of Aadhar card of deceased P.Gangi Reddy i.e., Ex.R.1.
Wherein the year of birth of P.Gangi Reddy was shown as 1957.
The alleged accident has occurred on 20.06.2020.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased P.Gangi Reddy was 63 years.

Hence,
the age of the deceased P.Gangi Reddy to be taken at 63 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.

18. In MFA.No.3661/2019(MV-D) between Smt. Shakuntala and others Vs. C. Nagesh and another,
Decided on 02.07.2021, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed as follows:
"7.We have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.

The only question which arises for our consideration in this appeal is with regard to the quantum of compensation.

The Supreme Court in 'NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS.
BIRENDER, 2020 SCC ONLINE SC 28, it has been held that the legal representative P.Subba Ratnamma vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93742737/

sentences.text: It has further been held that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being the legal representatives have the right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.
In the instant case, undoubtedly claimant No.1 is dependent on the income of the deceased.
However, claimant No.2 to 4 are the married and major sons and daughter of the deceased.
No evidence has been adduced by claimants No2 to 4 to show that the claimant No.2 to 4 were financially dependent on the deceased.
Therefore, in the absence of evidence, the Tribunal is justified in holding the claimants No.2 to 4 to be non-dependents.

8. The deduction of half of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses by the Tribunal cannot be faulted with as the claimant No.1 is the only dependent in view of the decision of the Supreme Court in SARALA VERMA VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AIR 2009 SCC 3104.

19.
Keeping the aforesaid principle in mind, this Tribunal would proceed to decide the case on hand by considering the evidence available on record.

The PW.1 deposed in his cross examination that petitioner No.1 is his mother, petitioner No.2 is his brother, he is B.Tech degree holder and searching for job and PW.1 has discontinued degree and searching for job.
Admittedly the petitioner No.2 and 3 were majors at the time of death of their father.
They have not adduced any to show that they were financially dependent on the deceased.
In fact the Ex.P.9 Patta book shows that the deceased has more than 4 acres land.
Hence this property is source for the petitioner No.2 and 3.
Therefore this Tribunal held that the petitioner No.2 and 3 were not depending on the income of the deceased at the time of accident and petitioner No.1 was wholly dependent on her husband's income.
20. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
21.
The deceased has left behind him, his wife and sons.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents to the conventional heads and the petitioner No.1 is considered as wholly dependent to all heads.

sentences.text: At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others). Wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced @ 10% in every three years."
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are sons of the deceased.
Petitioner No.1 have to live remaining part of her life in the absence of her husband and the loss of a husband full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to husband.
Petitioner No.2 and 3 have to live remaining part of their life in the absence of their father and the loss of a father full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to sons.

Therefore, petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each under the head of loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/-
towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/- towards funeral expenses.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
22.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and 2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased and they lost the love and care of deceased.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
23. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
24.
It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was notionally fixed at Rs.14,500/- p.m. in the year-2020.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "

sentences.text: Wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary if the deceased is more than 60 years there is no addition to be made".
In this Petition, the deceased was aged 63 years at the time of accident.
Hence, there is no addition towards future prospects.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.14,500/-.
25.
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 7.

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
But in the case on and as discussed above the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are major sons of deceased.
Hence petitioner No.2 and 3 are not considered as dependents of deceased.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 was wholly depending upon her husband's income.
Hence, 50% of the income of the deceased deducted towards his personal income.

26. After deducting half towards his personal expenses in Rs.14,500/- it comes to Rs.7,250/-
(Rs.14,500-7,250) and multiplier applied is 7 which comes to Rs.6,09,000/- (7,250 x 12 x 7).

Thus,
the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,09,000/- towards loss of dependency.

27. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:

Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.8,34,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

28. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.TN-18-AU-4158.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the "Affirmative" and issue No.3"Partly in the Affirmative".
29. Issue No.4 :
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,34,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents No.1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,34,000/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.1 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
